Verifier notes and special checks

Hasche-Mann is one printed page with four piano systems and 21 bars. Every bar is a complete bar of two quarter-note beats in 2/4, and both staves carry two sharps. The upper staff opens in the treble clef and the lower staff opens in the bass clef; the same clefs are reprinted at the start of each later system, and no clef change is printed. The first bar carries the opening signature. A forward repeat stands at the start of the ninth bar. The twentieth bar is the first ending and closes with an end-repeat. The twenty-first bar is the second ending and closes with the final barline. The system crops contain the notation, including the ending brackets, slurs, and dynamics. The page number and the title sit above the first system.

  • System 1, first bar: Is the first bar a complete bar of two quarter-note beats, with the 2/4 signature and two sharps? Yes. The 2/4 and two sharps are printed after the opening clefs, and the bar is filled by two groups of four sixteenth notes.
  • System 2, between the third and fourth bars: Is the heavy barline a forward repeat, and does it open the next bar rather than add an extra bar? Yes. Repeat dots stand to the right of the thin stroke, on both staves. There are no dots on the left. It is the start of the ninth bar.
  • System 4, twentieth bar: Does the first-ending bracket close with an end-repeat? Yes. The bracket marked 1. covers that bar. Repeat dots stand to the left of the thin-thick barline.
  • System 4, twenty-first bar: Is the last bar a complete second ending closed by a final barline? Yes. The bracket marked 2. covers that bar. A thin stroke and a thick stroke close it, with no repeat dots.
